pr_title: Change lists to reflect added and removed users retroactively
pr_body:
Add users' posts into lists after adding them, and remove upon removing. Makes lists usable right away instead of having to wait for people to publish a new post.

___

Fix #16290, fix #13687
pr_comments:
> I need to review it more thoroughly, but I think this does not remove replies from list members to accounts that have just been removed from the list.

That being said, this is not new and I think the same issue occurs in the Home timeline. So this can safely be considered separately.

issue_context.title: Lists do not update even when relationship is updated
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem 

#### Blocks
1. Block or be blocked by someone
2. Note that their statuses are still visible in the list despite the follow relationship being broken

#### Mutes
1. Mute someone
2. Their posts are removed from the column
3. Refresh the page
4. The posts are back

#### Unfollows
1. Unfollow someone
2. Note that their statuses are still visible in the list despite the follow relationship being broken

### Specifications

mastodon.social v3.1.3
comments:
I think lists aren't handled the same way as the home timeline out of performance concerns, but toots from blocked people remaining in the list sure is an issue.

Handling block and mutes would basically amount to changing `FeedManager#clear_from_timeline` and `FeedManager#unmerge_from_timeline` to handle lists as well. But if we do that, we probably want them to be able to apply to only a specific list as well in order to handle past statuses when adding/removing someone to the list.

review_comments:
Why use a string for `type` here? In ruby a symbol would be customary and also save a tiny bit of memory / performance overhead.

Much less important, but it might be nice to use keyword arguments for `type`.

This has to do with this being a Sidekiq worker, and Sidekiq serializing the parameters in JSON. Worker parameters are basically hashes and strings and cannot be anything else. It also does not support keyword arguments, and will pass a hash instead.
See `MergeWorker` above: I think `'home'` should be a symbol and think that maybe keyword arguments might be a nice touch.
